fields.title: From one cheaper forward pass to an auditable long-term research loop
fields.thesis: ROCS removes duplicate computation within a request. Rec-Distill moves expensive teacher knowledge into training. Effective Training Time tracks training lifecycle losses. FORTE controls feature retirement risk. Self-Evolving RecSys links proposals, experiments, and online feedback over time. They optimize different timescales; lower GPU cost, feature removal, and automated proposals are not evidence of recommendation gains.
fields.axis_0: Training, within-request inference, and long-term research costs
fields.axis_1: Dependencies and consumers that must stay consistent under reuse or deletion
fields.axis_2: Connecting offline gates, retraining, and real online feedback
fields.axis_3: How failed gates and negative results inform later decisions

fields.position: Encodes a user request once under candidate isolation, then scores candidates via deferred DCA interaction. Production IKBO broadcasts the request representation within the kernel.
fields.tradeoff: Sharing requires a candidate-independent user representation. Local work does not reproduce GLM/IKBO CUDA kernels or production clusters. Analytic reuse is not measured throughput.

fields.position: Materializes raw logits from the teacher's own forward pass, with sampling correction on the student side. The main tower trains only on true labels and serves; the auxiliary tower takes task and distillation losses and shares the backbone.
fields.tradeoff: Extra teacher and auxiliary-tower training lowers deployment burden, but a stronger teacher does not guarantee student gains. Align teacher/student probability spaces and compare against a same-budget student.

fields.position: Divides training time that consumes new data by end-to-end wall time, attributing losses to initialization, compilation, checkpointing, publishing, and recovery.
fields.tradeoff: Higher ETT is not higher model accuracy or GPU busy time. The local component decomposes lifecycle phases and ownership, not recommender capability.

fields.position: Perturbs dependencies in the frozen model, screens all heads and time windows, then retires features through joint ablation, real retraining, online experiments, and consumer lineage audits.
fields.tradeoff: Weak single-feature dependence does not imply safe joint removal. No candidate passed every gate in the local three-seed A100 run, so the baseline remained. Completing the process does not establish gains from deletion.

fields.position: An inner research agent proposes optimizers, architecture, and rewards and executes tools. An outer state machine enforces constraints, offline gates, and real A/B promotion; conclusions return to a journal.
fields.tradeoff: Executable experiments and independent evaluation are necessary. A proposal or registered name is not a capability. Small local tests do not replace production feedback, and active exploration does not waive gates.

fields.title: Charge costs to the right stage
fields.body: ROCS shares user encoding across candidates in one request, saving online duplicate work. Rec-Distill moves the larger model's influence into training and deploys a lightweight main tower, which may increase training work. ETT measures the share of end-to-end training advancing on new data, not request latency or device utilization. The three metrics may improve together or trade off; record the stage where each change acts.

fields.title: Automated research must be able to choose no change
fields.body: FORTE puts cost-saving proposals through quality and lineage gates. Retaining the original model when no candidate passes is a valid result. The Self-Evolving RecSys outer state machine also cannot treat completion of an inner experiment as production readiness. ETT reminds us to count failure recovery and duplicate work. Long-term memory should retain failure reasons, budgets, and consumer constraints, not merely names of successful proposals.

fields.question: ROCS and Rec-Distill both lower online cost. Why not add their savings directly?
fields.answer: ROCS eliminates repeated shareable encoding within a request. Rec-Distill changes the deployed model and leaves teacher and auxiliary work in training. The distilled architecture may change the shareable fraction, while kernels and bandwidth affect latency. Measure the combined path instead of multiplying or adding independent speedups.
fields.example: A student with much lighter user encoding may leave less duplication for ROCS to remove. Extra teacher training does not appear in per-request latency.

fields.question: Why might Effective Training Time be low even when the GPU stays busy and ROCS speeds up requests?
fields.answer: ETT counts only training time consuming new data in the numerator. Its denominator includes setup, compilation, checkpointing, publishing, and recovery. GPUs can be busy in those phases, and ROCS targets online inference rather than training. Attribute losses by phase and owner, not device busy time or inference latency.
fields.example: If 8 of 10 wall-clock hours train on new data and 2 compile or recover, ETT is 80% even if the GPU is fully occupied for the remaining 2 hours.

fields.question: If two features show almost no loss under separate FORTE perturbations, why can't a research agent delete both?
fields.answer: The features may back each other up; deleting one leaves the other signal, while deleting both exposes non-additive loss. FORTE also requires joint ablation, retraining, and an audit of all consumers. Send the proposal through actual Self-Evolving RecSys gates and retain failures in the journal instead of inferring safety from single-feature tests.
fields.example: A brand ID and a brand word can both identify the brand. Deleting either may barely matter, while deleting both hurts a sparse task. This is illustrative, not a paper measurement.

fields.question: If a Rec-Distill student scores slightly better offline and a research agent journals it, has it completed the launch loop?
fields.answer: No. Check student sampling correction, main and auxiliary roles, and matched budgets so the gain is not a protocol change. Then require independent validation and applicable online gates under the Self-Evolving RecSys outer controls. A journal preserves auditable runs and conclusions but does not grant promotion or replace execution evidence.
fields.example: If AUC changes after adjusting the student's negative sampling rate, repair any mismatch with the teacher logits' probability space before comparing. A “distillation succeeded” entry cannot fix it.

fields.summary: Initial version: compared ROCS, Rec-Distill, Effective Training Time, FORTE, and Self-Evolving RecSys. Added analysis and questions on the stages where costs occur and the dependencies that must remain consistent for sharing or deletion.
